description.text:
impulse:	no filtering - each output pixel equals some input pixel
linear:	linear interpolation between pixels
cubic:	smooth interpolation between pixels
Keys:	cubic a=.50, approximates sinc (*)
Simon:	cubic a=.75, continuous 2nd derivative (*)
Rifman:	cubic a=1.0, lots of sharpening (*)
Mitchell:	mix of sharpening and smoothing (*+)
Parzen:	approximating B-spline (+)
notch:	hides moiré patterns (+)
Lanczos4:	good for scaling down (*)
Lanczos6:	good for scaling down with some sharpening (*)
sinc4:	good for scaling down with a lot of sharpening (*)
(*) has negative lobes, can produce values that are outside the range of the input pixels.
(+) not interpolatory, changes pixels even when no movement.

description.plain_text: The SplineWarp node enables the user to generate arbitrary warpings of an input image through the use of pins and roto splines. Either can be placed in the frame to define source and destination regions. Any curve can also be marked as a boundary to prevent warping outside of the defined area. Correspondence points can be created along the splines. These points pair up locations on the A and B splines to provide control over how the image is warped. They can also be used to increase warping accuracy in selected areas since each segment is subdivided by the curve resolution. The curves panel presents a hierarchical stack/list interface of the curves and pins for managing the warp effect. Both warping and morphing can be accomplished with this node by keying warp and mix parameters. If there is no B image provided, then the mix parameter is ignored. The output is produced by warping images between the A and B markers by the warp amount and mixing the warped A and B images by the mix amount. The A image is warped from the A positions towards the B positions by the warp amount (0 to 1 equals 0 to 100%). The B image (if supplied) is warped from the B positions towards the A positions by 1-warp. The results are then mixed based on the mix parameter (0 = A, 1 = B, .5 = 50% of each). NOTE: At the moment only the first hard boundary curve affects the warp, other hard boundary curves are ignored! Hard boundary curves most also be closed.
